newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican soybean meal sales down on oversupply - ASA.
newsitem.headline: Mexican soybean meal sales down on oversupply - ASA.

text.p: Mexican soybean meal sales are down and an oversupply situation is looming, the local offices of the United Soybean Board (USB) and the American Soybean Association (ASA) said Wednesday.

"Crushers are stockpiling meal and some of the large crushers have reduced production volumes because of this fact. Local soybean meal prices are still at 2,600 pesos per tonne (about $331.00)," the USB/ASA said.
"There is a new crusher in Mexico (Cargill) and there is more supply of meal than demand," they added.

"The livestock industry is showing signs of increasing populations on feed, but livestock numbers are not growing at a rate fast enough to keep up with the rate of crush. We are oversupplied on meal which will force some crushers to slow down the volume of beans processed," they said.
Cargill opened its $30 million soybean processing plant at Tula in Hidalgo state in February. It is designed to process 1,500 tonnes of soybeans per day.
